title: A Orchard for the Postcard
premise: Wren Thackeray, a wedding planner whose own engagement ended in a courthouse parking lot, agrees to pose as the girlfriend of orchard owner Callum Reyes at his family's harvest reunion—strictly business, she tells herself, until dessert arrives and her heart forgets the arrangement. But Callum's family orchard is entangled in a land-grab scheme run by Wren's most powerful client, and the postcard that started it all—a decades-old love note mailed to the orchard—hides a truth about who really owns the land. When Wren discovers her firm built its reputation on burying exactly this kind of evidence, she must choose between the career that defines her and the man who makes her believe love can be present tense. She burns her professional bridges, testifies with the postcard in hand, and stays past the last train—choosing belonging over safety as the orchard blooms into their shared future.
about_author: Lior Pemberton is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent seven years planning other people's perfect days before trading ballrooms for blank pages. They write romance about people who build beautiful things for strangers while quietly dismantling their own walls.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Opening at a lavish wedding she's orchestrating, Wren reveals her cynicism through flawless execution and zero belief, flashing back to her broken engagement. When her boss assigns her the firm's biggest client—a developer circling an orchard property—she accepts without question. Emotional beat: armor presented as competence; the reader sees the crack before she does.

chapters.title: A Favor in Writing
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Desperate to face his family's reunion without pitying looks, Callum finds Wren through a wedding expo where she's working a booth. He offers payment for one weekend of pretending. She refuses—then finds the old postcard tucked in his proposal folder, a love letter addressed to the orchard from 1974, and curiosity overrides caution. Beat: two guarded people negotiating intimacy as a transaction.

chapters.title: Reunion Rules
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Arriving at Reyes Orchard, Wren meets Callum's sprawling, warm, intrusive family—including his grandmother Marisol, who wrote the postcard, and cousin Dani, who suspects everything. Wren performs the girlfriend role too well, memorizing details she shouldn't care about. Beat: belonging begins as performance and malfunctions into something real by the bonfire.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The reunion dinner: Marisol tells the story behind the postcard—her lost love, the land deed her brother signed away under pressure. Dessert becomes a near-kiss between Wren and Callum, interrupted by a call from Wren's firm: the developer wants her on-site scouting the orchard. Beat: desire and dread arrive in the same hour.

chapters.title: What the Client Pays For
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Back in the city, Wren digs into the developer's file and finds her own firm's fingerprints: decades of buried deeds, silenced families, the same playbook aimed at the Reyes orchard. Her mentor warns her off with chilling kindness. Beat: loyalty to her career curdles into complicity; the theme of power's corruption turns personal.

chapters.title: Staying Past Closing
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum returns to the city unannounced, and he and Wren spend a real, unscripted night together—no contract, no audience. Morning brings honesty: he tells her about the eviction notice; she almost tells him what she knows and doesn't. Beat: genuine intimacy achieved, immediately shadowed by her secret.

chapters.title: The Deed in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren steals into her firm's archives and photographs the original 1974 transfer documents proving Marisol's brother was coerced—the postcard's recipient was the notary who refused to sign. Her boss catches her leaving. Beat: point of no return; truth chosen over loyalty, with consequences looming.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren arrives at the orchard to warn them, but Dani has found Wren's original contract and exposes her employer in front of the family. Callum feels betrayed; Marisol, quietly, asks to see what Wren brought. The developer's crew arrives early to break ground. Beat: climax of betrayal and trust colliding on the eve of destruction.

chapters.title: Everything the Postcard Promised
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Climax. At the county hearing, Wren testifies, presenting the documents and Marisol's postcard, torching her career publicly when her firm's lawyer tries to discredit her. The injunction holds; the developer withdraws. Callum, watching her choose them, crosses the room. Beat: power confronted, truth vindicated, love declared in front of everyone.

chapters.title: Present Tense
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, epilogue-like. One year later: Wren plans only weddings she believes in, co-running events at the restored orchard. Marisol's postcard hangs framed above the tasting room. Callum proposes badly and perfectly among the blossoms; Wren says yes in the present tense. Beat: belonging earned, corruption refused, love no longer kept in the past.
